consensus_summary: Bread primarily symbolizes Jesus Christ as the Bread of Life and his body in the Eucharist/Lord's Supper, with complementary senses including God's provision, the Word of God, fellowship, and purity (unleavened).
book_summary: Bread symbolizes the word of God; unleavened bread is pure doctrine and leavened bread is corrupting doctrine.
consensus_core_identification: Christ himself (Bread of Life / eucharistic body)
book_core_identification: the word of God / pure vs. corrupting doctrine
boundary_disagreement: Consensus treats Word-of-God and pure-doctrine readings as secondary or complementary layers under a christological primary; the book elevates Word/doctrine as the sole core and omits Christ/Eucharist entirely.
material_contradiction: Book replaces the consensus primary referent (Christ/body of Christ) with a different referent (word of God/doctrine); both cannot stand as the core identification of the same symbol in the same sense.
rationale: Minimum cores differ: consensus centers on Christ as Bread of Life and eucharistic body (John 6; Last Supper texts), while the book centers exclusively on the word of God with a leaven=doctrine gloss. Word-of-God and unleavened-purity appear only as listed alternatives in the consensus, not as its primary identification; adopting the book therefore requires rejecting/replacing the consensus core rather than merely narrowing its boundary.
strongest_objection: The book entirely omits the dominant, cross-traditional christological and eucharistic identification (John 6; institution narratives) that the consensus treats as primary.
